ruleName: Long-form policy article: an inline glossary-term tooltip (Emissions Trading System) opens downward on hover/focus with no Esc dismiss, landing on the first ~3 lines of the next body paragraph. Method 2 absent, so Method 1 is the only path — and it obscures meaningful body text.

RTL (Arabic) API-reference docs: a dotted-underline glossary term 'cursor' shows a hover-only tooltip on a non-focusable span that covers the curl example block. A document-level Escape handler exists but its dismiss branch is gated on document.activeElement being a text input (copied from the filter box's clear-on-Esc behavior); while hovering the term nothing is focused, so the guard is false and Escape is inert.

SaaS analytics dashboard: a '?' badge on a conversion KPI opens a definition popover that covers the device-breakdown list. The popover is hoverable and persistent, but its only dismiss affordance is a close '×' button positioned INSIDE the popover, reachable only by Tab-ing focus off the trigger and into the additional content. No Escape handler and no toggle-on-trigger.

Summit & Pine outdoor-gear product page (Trail Runner GTX): color swatches show the color name in a hover bubble that has no focus path (swatch:hover .hover-name, no :focus equivalent) — superficially the same failure. But the color name is already printed as a persistent visible <span> under each swatch AND is each radio's accessible name (aria-label='Pine' etc.). The hover bubble is aria-hidden and purely redundant, so the missing focus path deprives no one of additional perceivable content. Redundancy decoy → PASS.

Patient-portal medication list: an 'interactions' pill on Warfarin opens a drug-interaction warning box that covers the dosage text. An Escape handler exists but is bound to the trigger button; the trigger's own click handler calls this.blur(), moving focus to document.body, so the keydown never reaches the handler and Escape is inert while the box obscures the dose.

SaaS billing page: a "?" help button beside "Seat overage" shows a custom tooltip positioned 30px BELOW the trigger, separated by a transparent .gap spacer (pointer-events:none). Show/hide is bound only to the trigger button's mouseover/mouseout; the tooltip has no hover handler and is not a descendant of the trigger. Moving the pointer down to read the tooltip crosses the gap, fires mouseout, and the tooltip vanishes before the pointer reaches it.

Banco Aurora high-yield savings page: a circular info 'i' icon next to '4.35% APY' reveals a hover-only popup disclosing a material tiered-rate caveat (4.35% only up to $250,000; above that 0.50%) found nowhere else on the page. The trigger is a non-focusable <span> with only mouseover/mouseout handlers, so keyboard, switch, and magnifier users never see the cap.

The Tidewater Review economics article: FOMC and bps are plain abbr title= (native, UA-controlled, out of scope / PASS), while GDP looks identical (same dotted underline) but is an abbr.gloss wrapping a span.bub author tooltip that JS reveals on hover/focus. The author bubble is pointer-events:none with no Escape handler. Two visually identical abbreviations, different owners — only the GDP one is governed by 1.4.13, and it fails; the reviewer must attribute each bubble element-by-element.

Loom Analytics campaign dashboard: the Conversions KPI card has a focusable '?' <button> whose tooltip explains a non-obvious 7-day post-click attribution model (why the number is lower than the ad platform's 28-day count). The button is a real tab stop with aria-label, aria-describedby, and a visible focus ring, but the JS binds the reveal only to mouseover/mouseout and never to focus/focusin, so focus produces no tooltip.

Community forum thread: a GitHub/Twitter-style profile "hover card" appears when hovering a username. It is rendered into a detached portal layer (#hovercard-layer, sibling of the content) positioned 12px below the username. Show is delayed 180ms (hover-intent); hide is immediate on the username's mouseleave; the card has no mouseenter of its own. Moving the pointer down to the card crosses the 12px transparent gap, fires mouseleave, and the card vanishes instantly.

PASSING counter-fixture. Higher-ed LMS reading with a '[1]' footnote reference that opens a citation popup on hover AND keyboard focus, deliberately overlapping the paragraph below (so Method 1 is not relied on). A document-level Escape handler hides the popup while focus REMAINS on the '[1]' button, and activating the trigger also toggles it closed — both SCR39-allowed dismissals.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-triggered glossary tooltip persists continuously while the trigger is held without prematurely disappearing on a timer.
The tooltip content remains visible for the entire duration the trigger is hovered or focused without self-withdrawing.

ruleName: Pharmacy prescription page: a glossary term <dfn> ("contraindication") shows a definition pop-up that DIRECTLY overlaps/adjoins the term (top:-2px, no gap) — visually the passing arrangement the Understanding describes. But the pop-up carries pointer-events:none and reveal is keyed only to the term's :hover, so moving the pointer onto the pop-up means the cursor is no longer counted as over the term, :hover collapses, and the content vanishes. Adjacency is present but the content is not actually hoverable.

Online-banking transfer-limit screen: a round 'i' info button shows a tooltip on hover AND keyboard focus that overlaps the help paragraph and the Continue button. The tooltip is keyboard-reachable (meets 2.1.1) but there is NO Escape handler, no documented shortcut, and activating the trigger does not toggle it off — the only way to clear the obscuring content is to move focus/pointer off the trigger.

Healthcare new-patient intake form: a 'What's this?' help popover on the Insurance Member ID field opens down-right with no Esc dismiss and overlaps the next field's required asterisk + label (Patient date of birth) and the input being filled.

Ledgerline invoicing toolbar: every button (Save/Export/Send/Duplicate) carries only a native title= attribute (e.g. title='Save your work'). There is zero JavaScript and no author popup DOM, so the hover bubble is rendered entirely by the user agent. This is the out-of-scope boundary anchor: visually similar to the author-built failing cases, but UA-controlled and therefore inapplicable / PASS by exclusion.

E-commerce garden-seed product page with pill-badge triggers; on hover/focus each reveals a role=tooltip with multi-sentence guidance. The auto-dismiss is implemented entirely in CSS — a @keyframes peekThenVanish animation with animation-fill-mode:forwards drives the popup to opacity:0 after ~3.5s while the badge is still hovered/focused; there is NO setTimeout/setInterval anywhere. Verified: opacity 1 at 0s -> opacity 0 at 4s while still hovering.

RTL Arabic e-commerce product page: a size-guide tooltip authored with physical left:0 does not mirror under dir=rtl and opens on top of its own trigger button, covering the label 'دليل المقاسات'. No Esc dismiss. Obscures the trigger itself — FAIL.

Government DMV registration-renewal wizard: focus-triggered help bubbles (role=tooltip) under the Plate and VIN fields. A single global setInterval(...,5000) clears any visible bubble every 5 seconds, so the VIN help vanishes while the field still has focus and the user is mid-task. Verified: visible on focus -> display:none at 6s while document.activeElement is still #vin.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus-revealed helper tooltip remains visible indefinitely while focus is held on the input and does not self-withdraw on a timer.

ruleName: The Tideline Review newsletter-signup promo (Privy/Mailchimp-style) appears over a dark scrim as a centered card. It looks modal and the developer moved initial focus into the email field, but there is NO focus trap and the background was never made inert/aria-hidden. Tabbing forward from the email field walks past Subscribe onto the article's 'Search the archive' input and button, hidden under the scrim; Shift+Tab leaks too.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order follows a logical and predictable sequence through the controls, preserving the meaning and operation flow.

ruleName: Meridian Bank wire-transfer form: focusing the high-risk Amount field opens a modal security step-up dialog (role='dialog' aria-modal='true') that dims the page, moves keyboard focus to its confirm button, traps Tab, and is dismissed via Escape/Cancel. Superficially this is content appearing on focus (the 1.4.13 trigger pattern), but modal dialogs are explicitly out of scope — the correct disposition is NOT-APPLICABLE to 1.4.13 (evaluate under 3.2.1 On Focus). This is the N/A modal carve-out anchor.

Government parking-permit form: a "?" help tooltip beside the "Parking zone" select, built correctly as the PASS anchor on the same component family. Trigger and tooltip share one wrapper (.help) whose box encloses both; reveal is keyed to the wrapper's mouseenter/mouseleave and focus-within. The tooltip is adjacent/overlapping (4px overlap, no gap), has pointer-events:auto and its own mouseenter, a 120ms hide delay tolerates the sub-element transition, and Esc dismisses it. A continuous pointer path from button to tooltip keeps the content visible.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-revealed tooltip remains persistent while the trigger is hovered without self-withdrawing on a timer.
The hover-triggered tooltip persists without self-withdrawing while the trigger remains hovered.

ruleName: E-commerce checkout (Northwind Outfitters) with two side-by-side boxed sections — Billing address and Shipping address — each visually holding Full name/Street/Apt/City/Postal in order. The whole form is one CSS grid; the DOM emits the two addresses interleaved line-by-line (billing-name, shipping-name, billing-street, shipping-street, ...), so with no tabindex the keyboard focus zig-zags between the billing and shipping cards on every Tab.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order repeatedly alternates between individual input fields of the Billing address and Shipping address sections instead of completing each address group sequentially.

ruleName: RTL Arabic (lang=ar, dir=rtl) two-attendee conference registration (مؤتمر الابتكار التقني) with two grouped, headed cards — الحاضر الأول (Attendee 1, on the right per RTL) and الحاضر الثاني (Attendee 2, on the left) — each with full name, email, job title, dietary preference. The DOM interleaves the two attendees field-by-field, so with no tabindex keyboard focus alternates between the right (Attendee 1) and left (Attendee 2) cards on every Tab.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order alternates between two attendee registration cards for each individual field rather than completing one attendee's details before moving to the next.

ruleName: ATS job application (Talentforge) Background step, single-column layout with two stacked sections — Education (Highest degree, School/university, Graduation year) wholly above Work experience (Most recent job title, Most recent company, Years in role). The DOM interleaves the two sections row-by-row (education-degree, work-title, education-school, work-company, ...) and CSS grid pins each field into its section block, so with no tabindex keyboard focus jumps ~300px down to Work and back up to Education on alternate Tabs while a sighted user sees two clean stacked blocks.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Keyboard focus order scrambles the form structure by ping-ponging back and forth between fields in the Education and Work experience sections.

ruleName: Nonprofit contact form (Riverbend Animal Rescue) with a contact-message column (Name, Email, Message) on the left and a 'How did you hear about us?' checkbox group (Instagram, From a friend, Web search, Event or flyer) on the right. The checkbox divs are spliced between the contact fields in DOM source order, so with no tabindex the tab sequence is Name -> Instagram -> Email -> From a friend -> Message -> Web search -> Event -> Send — the Understanding document's own failing example recast as a contact form.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order alternates back and forth between the left-column message form fields and the right-column survey checkboxes, disrupting the logical flow and completion of the form.

ruleName: Round-trip flight search (SkyHop) with two vertically stacked, headed panels — Outbound flight (From, To, Depart date, Passengers) above Return flight (From, To, Return date, Cabin). The DOM emits the eight fields in alternating legs (outbound-From, return-From, outbound-To, return-To, ...) and CSS grid routes each field back into its panel, so with no tabindex keyboard focus bounces between the outbound and return legs on every Tab while a sighted user sees two clean stacked cards.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The keyboard focus order repeatedly ping-pongs between the Outbound flight and Return flight form sections, disrupting the logical workflow and section structure.

ruleName: Al-Nakheel Clinic (Arabic, lang=ar dir=rtl) 'Confirm appointment' modal. The developer hand-rolled the dialog (no native <dialog>) but did containment correctly: on open they set the background wrapper inert AND aria-hidden=true, and installed a keydown handler that wraps BOTH directions (Tab on last -> first, Shift+Tab on first -> last). In RTL the visual left/right is mirrored but Tab semantics are unchanged. Focus never escapes the modal in either direction. PASS boundary that directly contrasts case-01.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus remains properly contained within the open modal dialog across all tab stops.
The focus order follows a logical top-to-bottom and right-to-left sequence through the modal form fields and actions, preserving task meaning.

ruleName: E-commerce category sidebar: hovering a top-level category ("Camp & Hike") reveals a CSS-only flyout submenu offset to the right (left:230px against a 210px row, leaving a ~20px transparent corridor). The flyout is a DOM child of the category but not geometrically contiguous; reaching lower submenu items requires a diagonal down-and-right path that exits both hot-zones, ending the :hover state and collapsing the flyout before the cursor arrives.

Joint loan application (Meridian Credit Union) with two side-by-side boxed sections — Applicant and Co-applicant — each with Full name, Date of birth, Annual income, Employer. Visually near-identical to the failing dual-section cases, but each section is a real fieldset containing its own fields in order, so the natural DOM order keeps each group whole: all four applicant fields are tabbed before any co-applicant field (the G59 passing pattern). PASS counter-example included so a judge cannot pass the failing cases by merely detecting 'two groups exist.'

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order logically completes all fields for the primary applicant column before moving to the co-applicant column and finally the review button.

ruleName: Bakery (Birchwood Bakehouse) footer with a flex row of five social-media links. DOM order is Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Pinterest, YouTube; CSS `order` paints them Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, TikTok, Pinterest. No tabindex, no JS. Verified tab order (DOM) differs from visual left-to-right order, but the links are an orderless set.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focusable elements consist solely of an orderless set of independent social media links whose sequence conveys no meaning or task dependency, making WCAG 2.4.3 not applicable.

ruleName: Ticketing checkout where a decorative 'Payment details' text divider was made tabindex=0 (for a reveal-on-focus animation) and sits in source between the Card number input and the Expiry input, injecting a meaningless focus stop into the middle of the card-entry sequence.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order follows a logical top-to-bottom, left-to-right sequence through the checkout form fields, preserving meaning and operability.
An inoperable generic container stop interrupts the keyboard sequence midway through a coupled payment form.

ruleName: Joint mortgage pre-approval form (Northgate Mutual) rendered as two titled columns — Primary applicant left, Co-applicant right — built with CSS Grid. The DOM interleaves the columns field-by-field and grid-column placement sorts each into its visual column. No tabindex, no JS. Verified tab order ping-pongs Primary-name, Co-applicant-name, Primary-DOB, Co-applicant-DOB, ... across two interdependent applicants.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order alternates horizontally between the primary applicant and co-applicant columns rather than completing each applicant section in sequence.

ruleName: SaaS analytics cohort-retention grid with dotted-underline column-header terms; on hover/focus each reveals a role=tooltip definition. A scroll listener on the fixed-height, sticky-header scroller hides the popup the moment the user nudges the grid to read a lower row, although hover on the term is retained. Verified: visible before scroll -> hidden after scrollTop change.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-revealed tooltip remains persistently visible while the trigger is hovered and does not dismiss itself on a timer.
The hover tooltip remains persistently visible while the trigger is held and does not disappear on a timer.

ruleName: LMS course home (BIO 210): a wide main course-content column (module links + Start quiz) on the left and a narrow, UNRELATED site-wide 'Annual Fund' donation widget on the right. The donation aside is DOM-first but flex order paints it right. No tabindex, no JS. Verified tab order: donation amount, Donate now, THEN the course links/quiz — right column focuses first, but the columns are independent.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order traverses the independent fundraising sidebar in full before moving systematically through the main coursework content.

ruleName: Telecom line-activation wizard, post-submit error state. Phone field is digits-only; the retained value is the all-digit string '12025550143'. The visible, aria-describedby-associated error reads 'Mobile number is invalid. Remove letters and parentheses from your phone number, then try again.' — describing a cause (letters/parentheses) that is factually absent from the value. The real defect (an 11-digit string for a 10-digit field) is never described.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error message misidentifies the error by instructing the user to remove letters and parentheses from a value that contains only digits.

ruleName: Developer issue tracker (Forge) label-chip list. Each chip's × opens an alertdialog confirm; confirming deletes the chip and moves focus to the NEXT chip's × (falling back to the previous chip when the deleted one was last, and to '+ Add label' when none remain). This is the F85 tag-delete exception that must NOT be flagged. Cancel returns to the chip's × (chip survives).

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order follows a logical top-to-bottom, left-to-right sequence through the label controls and actions.
Focus correctly returns to the opener button after dismissing the revealed dialog.
Activating the control moves focus directly into the revealed content, satisfying the revealed content insertion requirement.

ruleName: Real-estate listing: the entire large Walk Score hero tile is the hover/focus trigger; its explainer popover is pushed away into the next column to avoid the trigger, but lands on the Monthly cost estimate breakdown. No Esc dismiss. Tests the large-trigger 'Method 2 only' nuance.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover tooltip obscures adjacent page content and cannot be dismissed with the Escape key or any other in-place mechanism without moving focus or pointer.
The hover-triggered tooltip remains visible when the pointer moves directly over it.
The hover-revealed tooltip persists while the trigger remains hovered and does not disappear on an automatic timer.

ruleName: Calverton DMV 'Confirm renewal & payment' modal. The developer used the modern recommended technique — set the page wrapper's inert=true and rely on inert (no JS trap) to contain focus. But a OneTrust-style cookie-consent banner was injected by the tag manager as a direct child of <body>, OUTSIDE the inerted #page wrapper, so its 'Accept all cookies' / 'Manage' buttons stay focusable. Tab off the dialog's last control and Shift+Tab off its first control both land on the cookie buttons.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus escapes the open modal dialog to background cookie banner buttons.
The recorded tab sequence traverses the active controls in a logical and meaningful order without scrambling the reading or operation flow.

ruleName: Job board / ATS profile (Hirelane) with an 'Edit profile' button opening a three-step modal wizard (Basics → Availability → Summary). Each step moves focus to its first field; the final step swaps Next for Done. Pressing Done commits the edited values, closes the wizard, and returns focus to the originating 'Edit profile' trigger — the same return as Cancel and Escape — the affirmative PASS for terminal-confirm dismissal.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The resting focus order follows a logical top-to-bottom, left-to-right sequence that preserves meaning and task operability.
Focus successfully returns to the 'Edit profile' opener button when the revealed modal is dismissed.
Activating the 'Edit profile' button immediately moves focus into the revealed modal dialog content.

ruleName: University admissions page: the 'Explore Northgate ▾' mega-menu button is in the header partial, but the mega-menu panel is emitted by the footer theme partial, so its markup sits near the end of the DOM while position:absolute;top:96px floats it up under the header to look attached; opening it only toggles .open/aria-expanded with no focus move, so the next Tab from the trigger goes to header/main-content links, not into the menu.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The resting tab sequence follows a logical, systematic reading order from the top utility links through the header, main content cards, contact section, and footer.
Focus is not returned to the opener button after dismissing the revealed navigation menu.
Revealed navigation content is neither focused upon opening nor inserted immediately adjacent to the trigger button in the focus order.

ruleName: Single-page e-commerce checkout (Maple & Thread). A flex column whose 'Place order & pay' submit block is authored first in the DOM but pushed to the visual bottom with order:99. No tabindex, no JS. Verified tab order: T1 = the submit button (at y=1213, the visual bottom), then Quantity, Shipping, Payment — so Tab reaches the irreversible commit before any field.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The checkout form's primary submission button is encountered as the first focus stop before any of the required form input fields.

ruleName: Municipal parking-permit page (City of Aldergrove): a left-hand 'Parking services' nav and a wide application form on the right. The nav is authored AFTER <main> in the DOM and CSS Grid (grid-template-areas) paints it left. No tabindex, no JS. Verified tab order reaches the main form (plate, zone, email, submit) FIRST, then the side-nav links — the Understanding's own passing source-order technique.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus sequence systematically completes the main application form before moving through the sidebar navigation links, preserving reading and operational meaning.

ruleName: B2B wholesale coffee order grid: 3x3 matrix of quantity inputs (rows=pack sizes, columns=blends). Visual layout is row-major but Tab walks column-by-column (all sizes of one blend before the next), achieved purely by column-major DOM source order + CSS Grid placement (no tabindex). Completing one product's full size-ladder at a time is a logical purchasing workflow.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order follows a systematic column-by-column traversal through the grid of order inputs before reaching the submit button, preserving the logical meaning and operability of the form.

ruleName: SaaS 'set your password' screen, post-submit error state. Password field holds a 12-character value (shown as 12 bullets); the visible associated error reads 'Password must be at least 8 characters.' The page's own requirements checklist marks 'At least 8 characters' as MET (green) and 'At least one number' as the only UNMET rule (red). The error asserts a length rule already passed; the actual unmet rule (digit) triggered rejection but is not the one described, so the error contradicts the page's own checklist.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The password field displays an incorrect error message that contradicts the retained value and misidentifies the actual validation error.

ruleName: Healthcare patient portal (Riverbend) medication list with per-row Remove and an alertdialog confirm. Cancel ('Keep it') correctly returns focus to the Remove trigger, but Confirm ('Remove') deletes the row, calls window.scrollTo(0,0), and focuses the first header nav link instead of the next/previous medication's controls — the logical neighbor F85 requires when the trigger is removed.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus escapes the open confirmation modal dialog to background elements on the page.
The resting tab order follows a logical top-to-bottom, left-to-right sequence through the header navigation and each medication item's actions.
Focus successfully returns to the opener button after the confirmation dialog is dismissed.
Activating the Remove button successfully moves focus into the revealed confirmation dialog, satisfying the insertion requirement.

ruleName: CONTROL / discrimination foil (PASS). Event-ticketing phone field, post-submit error state — near-identical component to case-01. The retained value is '(202) 555-CALL', which genuinely contains parentheses, a space, a dash, and the letters C-A-L-L. The field is digits-only and the visible associated error reads 'Phone number must contain only digits. Remove the letters, spaces, and parentheses (for example, enter 2025550143).' — a cause that DID occur and correctly describes this value's actual defect.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The input error is clearly identified and described in text directly associated with the field.

ruleName: Mortgage 'configure & compare rate locks' tool with two side-by-side columns (Plan A 30-yr, Plan B 15-yr), each stacking Loan amount / Down payment / Points. Positive tabindex row-interleaves the columns (A.amt=1,B.amt=2,A.down=3,B.down=4,A.pts=5,B.pts=6), so Tab ping-pongs left-right across the gutter, breaking each plan's must-be-completed-as-a-unit field group.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order ping-pongs between input fields across the Plan A and Plan B cards rather than completing each plan's inputs sequentially.

ruleName: SafeHarbor auto-insurance 'Quick Quote' wizard on one screen: numbered steps (1) About you, (2) Your vehicle, (3) Coverage & quote shown top-to-bottom with circular number badges. Panels are placed by CSS Grid grid-row but emitted in DOM order 3,1,2. No tabindex, no JS. Verified tab order: T1 = Step 3 coverage radio, T2 = 'Get my quote', then jumps up to Step 1 name/age/zip, then Step 2.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus lands in Step 3 ('Coverage & quote') and its submit button before moving to Step 1 ('About you') and Step 2 ('Your vehicle'), breaking the sequential multi-step form workflow.

ruleName: Brightpath LMS 'Submit Lab Report 3' modal opened with native dialog.showModal() (UA-managed inert + containment). Inside, the formatting toolbar is an APG roving-tabindex group (one Tab stop, arrow-key navigation), so the FORWARD Tab order and the BACKWARD Shift+Tab order are intentionally NOT mirror images — yet focus never leaves the dialog and every control stays reachable and operable. PASS counter-example for the 'backward need not mirror forward' limb (TT 4.F step 2d).

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus is properly contained within the open modal dialog with no tab stops escaping to background content.
The focus order follows a logical top-to-bottom reading and operation flow through the dialog's form controls and action buttons.

ruleName: Arabic RTL developer forum thread: each comment has a 'رد' (Reply) button; activating Reply on the first comment reveals a reply form whose markup is appended at the very end of the thread DOM (after every other post and the footer) by a framework rendering one shared form per thread; the toggle flips .open/aria-expanded only with no focus move, so the next Tab goes to 'إعجاب' (Like) and through the rest of the thread before reaching the textarea.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The resting focus order logically follows the document structure from the header navigation, through each article in vertical order, to the footer navigation, matching the right-to-left Arabic reading flow.
Activating the reply button reveals a form that is appended to the end of the focus order instead of being placed adjacent to the trigger or focused directly.

ruleName: Healthcare patient-portal blood-pressure intake. Side-by-side Systolic (value 118, normal) and Diastolic (value 135, out of range) number inputs. The error 'Diastolic must be between 40 and 120 mmHg.' is placed in the Systolic column under the Systolic input, and the Systolic input carries the red alert border; the out-of-range Diastolic has no message. No aria-describedby.

Pulsar Platform API reference (rate-limiting page): the abbreviation 'TBA' is expanded only inside a pure-CSS :hover bubble containing the load-bearing burst formula (2x rate for ~5s) stated nowhere else. The reveal is the selector abbr.term:hover .bubble with no JS, so keyboard focus structurally cannot reveal it; the author also set tabindex="-1", removing the <abbr> from the tab order.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover-triggered tooltip obscures underlying page text and cannot be dismissed using the Escape key or any in-place mechanism without moving the pointer.
The hover-revealed tooltip cannot be reached by the pointer because a 10px physical gap separates it from the trigger element, causing the content to dismiss upon mouse movement.
The hover tooltip remains visible indefinitely while the trigger is hovered and does not dismiss itself on a timer.

ruleName: Recipe "cook mode" view (Hearthline — slow-braised short ribs). Each numbered step's coloured badge was made a single focusable static element (span.badge.focusable[tabindex="0"]) so a "mark this step done" coachmark could appear on focus, but the step's real "Start … timer" <button> is nested INSIDE that same focusable badge, so every timed step (3 of them) yields two consecutive tab stops for one control.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus sequence follows a logical top-to-bottom reading and operational order through the recipe steps and final action.
Focusable generic wrapper elements immediately precede the interactive timer buttons they enclose, creating redundant and confusing sequential tab stops.

ruleName: PASS boundary: a clinical 'add a patient allergy' form containing two focusable non-interactive elements placed where they do NOT impede operation — a role=status region (tabindex=-1) after the Save button that focus moves to on save, and a focusable end-of-form review summary placed AFTER all inputs and the submit button.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order follows the logical top-to-bottom reading and form completion flow without scrambling the intended sequence.
The focusable summary section at the end of the form does not interrupt a sequence or wrap a duplicate control.

ruleName: Northwind Pharmacy refill queue: each status help icon shipped with a native title=, but a Bootstrap/jQuery-UI-style tooltip plugin strips the native title on load (removeAttribute('title')) and renders its own gray span.nwtip styled to mimic the native UA tooltip. The author bubble is pointer-events:none, toggled only on mouseenter/mouseleave of the 18px icon, with no Escape handler. Visually near-identical to the case-01 native tooltip, but author-owned, so 1.4.13 applies and it fails.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover tooltip appears in empty space without obscuring or replacing other content, qualifying for the WCAG 1.4.13 dismissal exemption.
The hover-revealed tooltip disappears when the pointer travels from the trigger toward the tooltip because there is an un-hoverable gap between them.
The hover tooltip remains visible while the trigger is hovered and does not self-withdraw on a timer.
The hover-triggered custom tooltip obscures underlying page content and cannot be dismissed without moving the pointer or keyboard focus.
The hover-triggered tooltip extinguishes when the pointer moves toward it due to an unbridged 7px physical gap between the trigger and the tooltip.
The hover-revealed tooltip remains persistent while the trigger is hovered without self-withdrawing on a timer.
The custom hover/focus tooltip is author-styled, overlays existing content, and cannot be dismissed with the Escape key or any other mechanism without moving pointer or focus.
The hover-revealed tooltip disappears when the pointer travels toward it because of a gap between the trigger and tooltip content.
The hover-triggered tooltip remains persistently visible while the trigger is held and does not disappear on a timer.

ruleName: RTL Arabic (lang=ar dir=rtl) membership address form. A 2-column x 3-row CSS grid holds Postal code (column 1, value 11564, flagged red) and City (column 2, empty). The postal-code error is placed by explicit coordinates into grid-column 2 row 3 — the City column's message slot — so on screen it sits under the empty City input. No aria-describedby.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error message contradicts the input value by claiming the postal code must be 5 digits when the field already contains exactly 5 digits ('11564').
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the city input field, making error identification inapplicable to this element.

ruleName: Restaurant ordering site: a top-bar 'Menu ▾' button reveals a navigation flyout (role=menu) that appears visually directly under the button but whose markup is the last element in <body>; the click handler flips .open and aria-expanded only, with no focus move, so the next Tab from the button goes to the first page link ('Start your order'), not the menu items.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The resting focus order follows a logical top-to-bottom and left-to-right sequence that preserves page meaning and operability.
Activating the menu button reveals navigation links at the end of the page focus order rather than immediately adjacent or receiving focus upon opening.

ruleName: CONTROL (discrimination boundary): the same Riverbend Library membership flow as case-01, but the genuine SUCCESS result after VALID input (Age 34, a real email). The server accepted the data and rendered a true confirmation — a read-only summary of the accepted values, a real membership number (RVB-2026-08831), and next steps — with no editable form re-displayed and legitimately no error message. Must be judged passed while case-01..05 are failed.

E-commerce seller console (Looma) orders table where every row has an identical Actions menu button (aria-haspopup/aria-expanded, role=menu/menuitem, accessible names, correct on-open focus). Three menus (rows 1,3,4) return focus to their trigger on close; the visually-identical twin on row 2 (#LG-90411) calls document.activeElement.blur() on close, dropping focus to document.body so the next Tab restarts from the sidebar nav. The page fails because of that one broken menu.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The resting focus order systematically traverses the sidebar navigation links from top to bottom before moving sequentially through the action buttons in the main orders table.
Focus does not return to the triggering Actions button on row 2 when its dropdown menu is dismissed, dumping focus to the document body instead.
Revealed content satisfies the insertion requirement by moving focus directly into the revealed menu upon activation.

ruleName: Self-paced LMS course outline (ordered list of Start + Module 1-4). Links carry positive tabindex 1,5,4,3,2, so Tab visits Start then Module 4,3,2,1 - reversing the visible, content-meaningful study sequence the page explicitly says must be done in order. Canonical F44 reversed-list pattern in a real course page.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order jumps from the course introduction directly to Module 4 and proceeds in reverse sequence through Modules 3, 2, and 1.

ruleName: Hotel booking review, post-submit error state. Check-in '2026-08-01', check-out '2026-09-25' (55 nights — check-out IS after check-in). The check-out field's visible associated error reads 'Check-out date must be after your check-in date.' — a relation that already holds. The form's own visible policy states 'Maximum stay: 30 nights'; the real, undescribed error is that a 55-night stay exceeds that cap.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was detected or surfaced for the Check-in field.
The check-out field displays an incorrect error message that contradicts the entered dates, failing to identify the actual input error.

ruleName: PASS counter-example: a nonprofit donation form laid out with CSS flexbox 'order' so the amount block sits visually on top while it is authored SECOND in the DOM. Positive tabindex 1-5 is used DELIBERATELY to restore the visually-meaningful entry order (amount -> custom -> name -> email -> Donate). Uses positive tabindex but PRESERVES meaning, so it must not be flagged.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order follows the logical and visual sequence of the donation form from top to bottom.

ruleName: Arabic-language (dir=rtl) clinic appointment form localized from an English template. In RTL the rightmost box is visually first (given name; day), but positive tabindex was numbered left-to-right (1,2,3...) for the original LTR layout and never updated. Tab thus visits family->father->given and year->month->day - the exact reverse of the right-to-left reading order.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The sequential focus order navigates through multi-part form fields in reverse order from left to right, conflicting with the right-to-left Arabic reading and logical input flow.

ruleName: News/editorial site (The Meridian) full-screen search overlay opened from the masthead. On open it sets aria-hidden=false and moves focus into the search input; on Escape/Close it re-applies aria-hidden=true and hides the overlay but never restores focus to the Search trigger, leaving focus unrestored (Chromium blurs the now-hidden input, so focus reverts to the document body) and the next Tab restarts from the top of the page.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus escapes the open search modal dialog and cycles through background page elements.
The resting tab order follows a logical top-to-bottom reading and operational flow through the header actions, navigation links, and article content.
Focus fails to return to the 'Open search' button when the search dialog is dismissed, instead resetting to the document body.
No focus insertion barrier was found because activating the search opener moves focus directly into the revealed dialog.

ruleName: Healthcare new-patient intake, post-submit error state. Date-of-birth field retains '03/14/2027', which already conforms exactly to MM/DD/YYYY. The visible associated error reads 'Date of birth is invalid. Please use the MM/DD/YYYY format.' — naming a constraint that is already satisfied. The actual error (a birth date set in the future) is never described, so the only guidance is a no-op fix.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The Legal name field is not in an error state and no error was triggered for this element.
The error message misidentifies the error as a format mismatch even though the field already contains a properly formatted date.

ruleName: Cedar Mutual Auto 3-step quote wizard silently advanced to 'Step 3 of 3, Review & buy' after an invalid ZIP ('0', too short) on Step 1 was swallowed — Step 2 (coverage options) was skipped because the rating engine had no usable ZIP. The review summary freezes the invalid ZIP '0' as read-only text and shows a placeholder premium '$—'; no error text appears. Cross-page silent-advance variant. LONG-TAIL; content-domain insurance quote wizard, APG stepper + dl review, lazy-validation persona.

Arabic RTL airline seat-selection page: a held seat (C٢) shows, on hover/focus, a role=tooltip with the live remaining hold time (Arabic-Indic countdown). The popup stays visible the whole time the hold is valid and the seat is hovered; when the countdown reaches zero the hold genuinely expires (seat released, message now false) and the popup is removed because its information became invalid. Verified: visible through countdown ٠٠:٠٧ -> ٠٠:٠٤, removed only after real expiry, seat no longer held, pay button shows 'hold timed out'.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The hover/focus-triggered tooltip can be dismissed in place by pressing Escape without moving focus or the pointer.
The hover-revealed tooltip directly adjoins and overlaps the trigger button without a gap, allowing the pointer to move onto the revealed content without dismissing it.
The additional content revealed on hover and focus persists for as long as the trigger remains hovered or focused.

ruleName: Government benefits-enrollment form (Step 2 of 4) where every field has explicit positive tabindex 1-8, but a later-added required 'Daytime phone' field was dropped in with NO tabindex. Because positive-tabindex elements are visited first, the un-indexed phone field is tabbed dead last, after the Submit button. The F44 edit-drift variant the technique itself describes.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order places the required 'Daytime phone' input field after the form submission buttons, disrupting the logical flow of completing the form.

ruleName: Artisan pottery e-commerce product page where a focusable div[tabindex=0][role=button] wraps a real <button> 'Add to basket', so Tab stops on the wrapper then the button — the same control appears to receive focus twice (the exact div[tabindex=0]><button> shape pictured in the Understanding note).

rubricVerdicts.summary: The resting focus order preserves meaning and operation flow, moving logically through the header navigation links, followed by the glaze selector and the add to basket action.
A redundant focusable wrapper receives focus immediately before the identical button it encloses.

ruleName: Hexagon Arena box-office 'Have a promo code?' jQuery-UI-style dialog. The developer moved initial focus in and restored it on close but never added a Tab wrap on the last control. Pressing Tab on the 'Apply code' button (the dialog's last control) follows DOM order to the page's first focusable element — a visually-hidden 'Skip to footer' skip-link — instead of cycling back to the first dialog control.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus is not contained within the open modal dialog and navigates to background page controls.
The recorded tab sequence follows a logical, predictable reading and operation order across both the main page structure and the promo code dialog.

ruleName: PASS boundary (hardest 'tedious vs impedes operation' line): a developer API reference sidebar where each category section header (Getting started / Core / Advanced) is a focusable static span[tabindex=0], adding an extra Tab stop per category. The stops are merely tedious — each label heads its OWN group, no link is duplicated, and no stop is wedged between two coupled controls.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order follows a logical and systematic sequence through the navigation sidebar and into the main content.
The focusable category headers in the navigation sidebar introduce groups of links without wrapping child controls or interrupting a coupled data-entry sequence.

ruleName: SaaS analytics dashboard (Metrico) 'Dashboard settings' modal. On open, focus correctly moves into the dialog; on close (via ×, Cancel, Save, or Escape — all routed through one closeDialog()), focus is dropped to document.body instead of returning to the 'Dashboard settings' trigger, so the next Tab restarts at the top-of-page header nav.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus escapes the modal dialog when Dashboard settings is opened, allowing keyboard users to tab into background page controls.
The resting tab sequence follows a logical, systematic order from the header navigation links to the main toolbar controls, preserving meaning and operability.
Focus is dumped to the document body rather than returned to the opener button after the Dashboard settings dialog is dismissed.
Activating the Dashboard settings button immediately shifts focus into the revealed content.

ruleName: E-commerce checkout payment row (Card number / Expiry / CVV) in a flex row. The CVV value '12' is the truly-invalid input, but the error 'CVV must be exactly 3 digits.' is rendered in the message slot under the Card number field, and the Card number input carries the red invalid border. No aria-describedby anywhere.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The flagged Card number field displays an error message for a completely different input (CVV).
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the expiry date field in the submitted form state.
The error for the CVV input is misattributed to the Card number field, with visual error flagging and the message rendered under Card number rather than identifying the error on CVV.

ruleName: Government SNAP-benefits two-column grid form. Row 1 has First name (left, filled 'Maria') and Last name (right, filled). After a failed submit the error 'First name is required.' is placed in the right-column cell directly under the Last name input, and Last name (not First name) gets aria-invalid=true. No aria-describedby links the message to any control.

rubricVerdicts.summary: First name was not flagged in error, so no error state applies to this input under WCAG 3.3.1.
The error message displayed beneath the flagged Last name field incorrectly states that the First name is required, failing to properly identify the error for this field.
No error was detected or flagged for the middle initial field.
No input error was triggered, flagged, or demonstrated for the Preferred name field.

ruleName: Real-estate listings results page: a toolbar 'Filters' button reveals a filter form (price/bedrooms/type) that is position:fixed to appear right beside the button on the left, but whose markup is the last element in the document after every listing and the footer; the toggle adds .open only, with no focus move, so the next Tab goes to 'Sort: Newest' and then through eight listing links before reaching the filter controls.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus order follows a logical and systematic sequence across the page header, controls, grid of property listings row-by-row, and footer.
Activating the Filters button reveals a filter form whose interactive controls are neither focused on activation nor placed immediately adjacent to the opener in the focus order.

ruleName: Bank reset-password screen redisplayed after rejecting a reused password; the field shows a red outline + a red CSS ::before key glyph and carries aria-invalid='true', but emits NO error text, aria-errormessage, or aria-describedby — nothing in words states what is wrong or why.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The field is flagged as invalid with a red border and aria-invalid attribute, but the error is not described in text.
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the 'Confirm new password' field.

ruleName: Boundary PASS counter-example: a coffee-roaster wholesale page where the 'Get the wholesale price list' button reveals a non-modal dialog whose markup is placed immediately after the trigger, so the dialog's email field is the very next node in source order; the visibility-only toggle is correct here and dismissal returns focus to the trigger.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The resting focus order follows a logical, predictable sequence from header navigation through main content cards to footer links.
Focus successfully returns to the trigger button when the revealed price list dialog is dismissed.
The revealed content is inserted immediately adjacent to its opener in the keyboard focus order upon activation.

ruleName: Municipal government portal: a 'Subscribe to alerts' button in a top announcement bar reveals a centered non-modal newsletter dialog whose markup is the last block before </body>; the open handler only toggles a CSS .open class and never moves focus, so after keyboard activation focus stays on the trigger and the next Tab lands on the first nav/content link, not the dialog.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The keyboard focus order follows a logical, systematic sequence across the page header, banner, main service grid, contact section, and footer.
When the 'Subscribe to alerts' dialog is dismissed, focus is dropped onto the document body instead of returning to the opener button.
Activating the 'Subscribe to alerts' button reveals a dialog whose interactive controls are neither placed immediately after the opener in the focus order nor focused automatically upon activation.

ruleName: City government primary nav: a 'Residents & Services' submenu opens on hover and on activation/focus of its toggle and covers the page banner and intro text. It carries aria-haspopup/aria-expanded/aria-controls, but the only way it closes is a document-level click outside the menu (pointer only) — no Escape handler and activating the toggle only re-opens it, so keyboard/magnifier users cannot dismiss the obscuring panel without moving focus away.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No additional content was triggered upon hovering or focusing the element, so dismissibility cannot be evaluated from the captured state pair.
No additional content or tooltip appears when hovering over the Government navigation item.
No hover or focus content is triggered by this navigation item, so no self-withdrawing persistence barrier exists.
No additional content or overlay is revealed on hover or focus of the Business navigation link.
Hovering over the Business navigation item does not reveal any additional content, so no 1.4.13 hoverability barrier is present.
No additional content is revealed on hover or focus that disappears on its own.

ruleName: HR 360-degree competency review: a 4x4 matrix where each cell is its own <input type=range> slider (rows=competencies, columns=rater perspectives Self/Manager/Peer/Direct report). Not a radio-group matrix, so focus order is governed by DOM source order. Visual layout is row-major but Tab walks column-major by rater (all four Self sliders, then Manager, ...) via column-major source order + CSS Grid (no tabindex). Assessing from one perspective at a time is exactly how a 360 instrument is completed.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The focus sequence systematically traverses the rating grid column-by-column (all Self ratings, then Manager, Peer, and Direct report, followed by Submit), preserving meaning and operability.

ruleName: Home-insurance quote wizard, step 2 Property: red role=alert summary says 'Please fix 2 things: Country must be selected. Year the property was built must be a 4-digit year'. Year built is genuinely flagged (value 'nineteen eighty'), but the Country control is a disabled <select> pre-set to 'United Kingdom' (locked because the product is UK-only) — greyed, non-focusable, no aria-invalid — and could not have produced input nor be corrected.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error summary falsely identifies an error on the Country field ('Country must be selected') even though the control is disabled, pre-selected with 'United Kingdom', and not in an invalid state.
No input error was triggered or demonstrated for the property postcode field.
The error for the year input is clearly identified in text directly below the field and in the error summary.

ruleName: Credit-union online-banking enrolment: red role=alert summary states 'Password must be at least 10 characters and include a number', but the Password field is valid (green, aria-invalid=false, meets the rule). The only flagged field is its sibling Confirm password (aria-invalid=true, red, 'does not match the password you entered'). The summary blames the wrong sibling and describes a different cause.

rubricVerdicts.summary: No error was flagged or demonstrated for the Username field, so 3.3.1 error identification is not applicable to this element.
The error summary banner incorrectly flags the Password field with a constraint requirement that its retained value already satisfies, while omitting the actual error.
The error summary misidentifies the error by claiming the password field failed requirements while omitting the confirm password field that was actually flagged.

ruleName: Retail account signup re-displayed after a failed submit; the email field holds a malformed address (jane.summit.example.com, no @) and the sole per-field error indicator is an error icon carrying a non-empty but uselessly generic alt="error".

rubricVerdicts.summary: The Full name input field is not in error, so error identification under WCAG 3.3.1 does not apply to it.
The invalid email field is flagged with a red border and a generic error icon, but the specific error is not identified in text.
No input error was detected or flagged for the password field, making error identification inapplicable to this element.

ruleName: Alumni reunion RSVP (en-GB); email ravi@@pembury.ac.uk (double @) and date 2024-07-18 (in the past) are both invalid, but a refactor cut-and-pasted the date row's error icon above the email row without updating it, so the email field sits beside an SVG whose aria-label="Date is in the past" — correct cause for the wrong field.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The Full name input is not in an error state and was not flagged as invalid.
The email address field's error is not identified in visible text and its associated programmatic description incorrectly states that the date is in the past.
The field is indicated as invalid solely via a red border and aria-invalid attribute, with no textual error description provided.

ruleName: Northbridge Bank 'Confirm transfer' modal (dim backdrop + centered card). A hand-rolled focus trap wraps only the FORWARD direction; the Shift+Tab branch was never written. Forward Tab is perfectly trapped, but Shift+Tab from the first control (the amount field) falls through to the browser default and lands on the page header's 'Log out' link behind the non-inert backdrop.

rubricVerdicts.summary: Focus escapes the open modal dialog during backward navigation to underlying header links.
The tab order follows a logical top-to-bottom sequence through the form fields and action buttons without scrambling meaning or operability.

ruleName: Brightwater Rivers Trust donation page bounced after the amount was submitted as $0.00 (below the stated $5 minimum) AND the required 'How often?' frequency radio group was left unselected; a warm 'Thank you for your generosity' banner sits above the re-displayed form with the bad amount retained and the radio group still empty and unflagged. Variant B with a second omitted required field. MID/long-tail; content-domain nonprofit/donation, fieldset radio group + currency input, fundraising-CMS persona.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The field is in an error state with an invalid retained value (0.00) and visual flagging, but the error is not identified in text.
No input error was flagged at rest or triggered for this radio input control.
The form is in an at-rest error state after submission, but the error is not identified in text for this required field.
The error on the required frequency radio group is indicated only by color and lacks a textual error message identifying the error.

ruleName: CONTROL (discrimination boundary): auction 'place a bid' form with the IDENTICAL red border + tint on the email field, but the error is also identified and described in text ('Email address is not valid.') tied via aria-describedby, with aria-invalid='true' and the decorative icon aria-hidden. Should pass.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The 'Your name' field is not in an error state, so WCAG 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to this element.
The input error is clearly identified in text and programmatically associated with the field.
No error was flagged or demonstrated for the maximum bid field.

ruleName: Restaurant catering-enquiry form: red role=alert summary lists three errors (Event date, City, Number of guests). Event date and Number of guests are genuinely flagged below, but the middle line 'City is required' names a field that does not exist anywhere on the form — the page collects a single free-text 'Venue name & full address' textarea with no City input, label, or control.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error for the Event date field is clearly identified in text both inline and within the error summary.
The venue name and address textarea is not in an error state and has no input error detected against it.
The error for the 'Number of guests' field is clearly identified in text with an accurate and specific inline error message.

ruleName: Conference call-for-papers form returned after a blank required 'Talk title'; the only error/required cue is the label turned red with a trailing CSS ::after asterisk. No message, no legend explaining the asterisk, no required/aria-required/aria-invalid.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The Full name input field is not in an error state and no error was detected or triggered for it.
The Date of birth field is not in an error state on this form.

The Vehicle registration field is not in an error state on this form, so error identification requirements do not apply to it.

ruleName: Nonprofit one-time-gift form; the donor entered 25000 (over the stated $10,000 online maximum) and the error is conveyed by a Material-Icons-style icon-font glyph whose aria-label is the literal ligature key "error_outline" — describing the picture, not the error.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The rejected gift amount field is flagged only by a red border and a generic error icon without any text identifying what the error is.
The field 'Name on card' is not in an error state and was not flagged or rejected.

ruleName: GOV.UK council-tax reduction form: top-of-form red error summary announces 'We found 2 errors' and lists Full name + Email, but both render filled and unflagged; the only field actually in error (Telephone, value 'ring me weekdays') has a red border, inline message and aria-invalid=true and is never named. Wrong count AND wrong fields named.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The error summary falsely identifies the Full name input as having an error when only the Telephone number field is in error.
The error summary at the top of the form fails to identify the telephone number error and misdirects users to other non-erroring fields.

ruleName: CONTROL (passing): flight-booking Passenger details step. Red role=alert summary states 'There are 2 problems' and lists exactly two G139 jump links — Email (→#email) and Date of birth (→#dob). ruleName: University admissions application wizard, step 3 Contact details: red role=alert summary lists two G139-style jump links. ruleName: Community allotment newsletter signup re-rendered after a failed submit; the invalid email field ('tom@') wears a 2px red border + red-tinted background as the SOLE error cue. No message, no aria-invalid, no hidden text anywhere conveys that an error occurred.

rubricVerdicts.summary: The field 'Name on your library record' is not in an error state, so WCAG 3.3.1 error identification does not apply to it.

ruleName: Healthcare patient-intake form (step 1 of 3); an impossible date of birth (31/02/1991) is flagged ONLY by a red exclamation-triangle SVG image with alt='' beside the field. No nearby/hidden text, aria-label, or aria-invalid conveys the error.
